HAND-MADE SAMPLE. This is NOT a House Research Organization document. hro.house.texas.gov refused connections from
the build machine on 17 Nov 2026, so this file copies only the STRUCTURE of an HRO bill analysis (its header, its
fixed headings in their usual order, a running page header). Every sentence under a heading was invented for the test.

HOUSE RESEARCH ORGANIZATION bill analysis                5/20/2025                SB 4 (2nd reading)
                                                                                  Bettencourt, et al. (Meyer)

SUBJECT:      Sample subject line: raising a school property tax break for homeowners

COMMITTEE:    Ways and Means — favorable, without amendment

VOTE:         11 ayes — sample names
              0 nays
              2 absent — sample names

SENATE VOTE:  On final passage (February 13) — 30-0

WITNESSES:    For — sample witness; Against — None; On — sample witness

BACKGROUND:   Sample background. Tax Code sec. 11.13(b) entitles an adult to an exemption from taxation by a school
              district of $100,000 of the appraised value of the adult's residence homestead.

DIGEST:       Sample digest. SB 4 would raise the school district homestead exemption from $100,000 to $140,000 and
              would entitle school districts to additional state aid for the revenue they would lose.

SB 4
House Research Organization
page 2

SUPPORTERS    Sample supporters' reason. SB 4 would lower school property taxes for homeowners at a time when rising
SAY:          home values have pushed tax bills up, and the state would cover what school districts lose.

CRITICS       Sample critics' reason. SB 4 would give nothing to renters and businesses, and it would commit the state
SAY:          to a large cost every year that could crowd out other spending when revenue falls.

OTHER         Sample second reason. Tax relief would be better delivered by lowering school tax rates, which helps every
CRITICS SAY:  kind of property owner.

NOTES:        Sample note. According to the Legislative Budget Board, the bill would have a negative impact of about
              $2.7 billion to general revenue related funds through fiscal 2027.
